    theorem LargeIndecomposable.unitRayEquivalent_square_of_same_ray {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [hlinear : CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [hlocal : ∀ (X : C), IsLocalRing (CategoryTheory.End X)] [hartinian : ∀ (X : C), IsArtinianRing (CategoryTheory.End X)] [hdistributive : HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k C] {X : C} (f f₁ f₂ : CategoryTheory.End X) (hf : f ≠ 0) (h₁ : UnitRayEquivalent f f₁) (h₂ : UnitRayEquivalent f f₂) :
    UnitRayEquivalent (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f f) (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f₁ f₂)

    If two consecutive morphisms lie in the same endomorphism ray, changing both representatives preserves the ray of their ordinary composite. The point is that the sole middle unit can be moved through one of the two copies using transit-or-cotransit.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.comp_eq_zero_iff_of_four_same_endomorphism_rays {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [hlinear : CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [hlocal : ∀ (X : C), IsLocalRing (CategoryTheory.End X)] [hartinian : ∀ (X : C), IsArtinianRing (CategoryTheory.End X)] [hdistributive : HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k C] {X : C} (f f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂ : CategoryTheory.End X) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hf₁ : UnitRayEquivalent f f₁) (hf₂ : UnitRayEquivalent f f₂) (hg₁ : UnitRayEquivalent f g₁) (hg₂ : UnitRayEquivalent f g₂) :
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f₁ f₂ = 0 ↔ CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp g₁ g₂ = 0

    Consequently, for a fixed nonzero endomorphism ray, either every pair of representatives composes to zero or none does. A singular length-two path therefore cannot repeat the same arrow.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.repeatedRayArrow_not_singular {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [hlinear : CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [hlocal : ∀ (X : C), IsLocalRing (CategoryTheory.End X)] [hartinian : ∀ (X : C), IsArtinianRing (CategoryTheory.End X)] [hdistributive : HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k C] [hpair : HasBGRSPairDichotomy C] {i : RayVertex (BGRSRayCategory C)} (a : i ⟶ i) :
    ¬(rayPathMap (a.toPath.comp a.toPath) = 0 ∧ ∃ (f : CategoryTheory.End i.obj.as) (g : CategoryTheory.End i.obj.as), unitRay f = ↑a ∧ unitRay g = ↑a ∧ CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f g ≠ 0)

    The "two arrows are distinct" clause needed by simultaneous singular normalization is already forced by distributivity: a repeated loop arrow has the same zero/nonzero composite status for every choice of its two representatives.

    A packaged arrow type lets the distinctness conclusion be stated even when the two consecutive arrows initially have different endpoint types.
